lines: In spoken Arabic, when switching from present tense to the past, verbs are are divided into 3 categories:

sections.heading: Normal verbs (3 consonants and more):
lines: Pronouns are also divided into 2 groups when switching to past:
• Huwwe, heyye,  humme
• Ana, inta, inti, intu, i7na.

sections.heading: How Do We Turn Normal Verbs to Past?
lines: 1. Remove the “ba” present prefix.
2. You then have the he past form of that verb.
3. Heyye: you add “at” to the end of the verb.
4. humme : you add “u”
5. Ana + inta: add “et” to the end.
6. Intu: add “tu”
7. i7na : add “na”
This category is divided into 2 groups:
#### “A” internal flip
This group flips the short vowels within the verb into “a”

sections.heading: 2. Middle Long Vowel Verbs Category
lines: Verbs in this category have a long vowel in the middle. E.g. bashoof, ba9eer, banaam, basaa3ed, etc.

sections.heading: How Do We Turn Middle Long Vowel Verbs into Past?
lines: • Remove the “ba” present tense prefix. Bashoof - ba = shoof.
• Flip the “oo” long vowel to “aa” = shaaf.
• Huwwe: the product of flipping the “oo” into “aa”
• Heyye: add “at” to the end. = shaafat.
• Humme: add “u” = shaafu.
• Ana + inta: go back to the base form (shoof) and shorten the “oo” long vowel to be only “u” then add the “et” to the end of the verb. = shufet.
• inti : add “ti” = shufti.
• Intu: add “tu” shuftu.
• I7na: add “na” = shufna.

sections.heading: Notes:
lines: • All middle long vowels flip to “aa” when switched to past.
• For longer verbs (3 consonants or more) that also have middle long vowel, these vowels don’t get shortened for I, you, and we, conjugations. E.g. saa3adet not sa3adet, and 2aatalti and not 2atalti.
• longer verbs that have “t” as the second consonant do get shorter though. E.g. 7tajet not 7taajaet, and rta7et and not rtaa7et.

sections.heading: 3. End Vowel and Short Verbs
lines: This category includes all verbs that end with a vowel (e.g. ba7ki, bamshi, etc.),and all short verbs (e.g. barudd, ba7ebb, etc.)

sections.heading: How Do We Turn Short and End Vowel Verbs into Past ?
lines: • Remove the “ba” present prefix. Ba7ki - ba = 7aki & ba7utt - ba = 7utt.
• For end vowels, flip the vowel to “a” and add another “a” to the middle for easier pronunciation. 7ki = 7aka
• For short verbs, only flip the middle vowel to “a” (you do not add an extra “a” to the end. 7utt = 7att.
• Huwwe: 7aka & 7abb.
• Heyye: add “t” for end vowel verbs and “at” for short verbs. = 7akat & 7attat.
• Humme” turn the “a” into “u” = 7aku, and add a “u” for short verbs. = 7attu.
• Ana + inta: add “ait” suffix to = 7akait & 7attait.
• Inti: add “aiti” suffix to the base verb. = 7akaiti & 7attaiti.
• Intu: add “aitu” suffix. = 7akaitu & 7attaitu.
• i7na : add “aina” suffix. = 7akaina + 7attaina.

sections.heading: Prepositions › Min | من
lines: Core functions: origin, source, starting point, comparison, cause. English: from / out of / than.
• Ana Bashte8el min el-bait | I work from home.
• Ba7eb el-shai aktar min el-2ahweh | I like tea more than coffee.
• Ana ta3ban min el-shu8ul | I'm tired from work.

sections.heading: Prepositions › 3ala | على
lines: Core functions: location, destination, time/event. English: on / at / to.
• El-akel 3ala el-tawla | The food is on the table.
• Ana baru7 3ala el-bait | I go home.
• Ana bashrab 3asir 3ala el-3asha | I drink juice at dinner.

sections.heading: Prepositions › Fi | في
lines: Core functions: inside something physically or conceptually (place, time, condition); "there is". English: inside / in / there is.
• Ana bashte8el fi America | I work in America.
• Ana banam fi-ellail | I sleep at night.
• Fi mushkeleh fi hai el-8assaleh | There is a problem in this washing machine.

sections.heading: Prepositions › Ma3 | مع
lines: Core functions: accompaniment, togetherness. English: with.
• Ana baru7 3ala el-shu8ul ma3 sadiqi | أنا بروح على الشغل مع صاحبي | I go to work with my friend.
• Huwwe byakol El-akel ma3 3aseer | هو بياكل الأكل مع عصير | He eats the food with juice.
• Humme byeeju ma3i | هم بييجوا معي | They come with me.

sections.heading: Prepositions › Bi | بِ
lines: Core functions: location/inside, means, instrument/tool, engagement. English: by / with / in.
• Ana baaji bi-lseyyara | أنا باجي بالسيارة | I come by car.
• Huwwe ma bye7ki bi-ltelefon | هو ما بيحكي بالتلفون | He's not speaking on the phone.
• Humme byaklu bi-el-shoakeh u el-sekkineh | هم بياكلوا بالشوكة والسكينة | They eat with a fork and a knife.

sections.heading: Prepositions › La | لَ
lines: Core functions: possession, recipient, purpose, end point. English: for / to.
• Hada el-ktab la-mehdi | هاد الكتاب لمهدي | This book is for Mehdi.
• Huwwe beynam min el-lail la-lsubu7 | هو بينام من الليل للصبح | He sleeps from night to morning.
• Ana bat3allam 3arabi la2dar a7ki ma3kom | أنا بتعلم عربي لأقدر أحكي معكم | I learn Arabic to be able to speak with you.
• Enti laazem te7kilo enno huwwe naaje7 | أنتِ لازم تحكيلو انو هو ناجح | You should tell him that he's successful.
• Hadi el moazeh eli mish elo | هادي الموزة الي مش الو | This banana is mine not his.

sections.heading: Noun possessives
lines: In spoken Arabic, possession is shown by putting two nouns next to each other. No apostrophes, no "of": main noun, then the owner.

sections.heading: Noun possessives › Proper nouns pattern
lines: Thing + name. No el- on the first noun; proper nouns make it definite.
• Mehdi's book = Ktaab Mehdi. California Street = Share3 California. John's shirt = Bloozet John.
If the first noun is feminine, add "t" to its end before linking.

sections.heading: Noun possessives › Nouns with pronouns pattern
lines: Thing + pronoun-ended noun. No el- on either noun.
• My hand's finger = Usba3 eedi. My friend's room = 8urfet sadiqi. My family's house = Bait 3ailti.

sections.heading: Noun possessives › Common / regular nouns pattern
lines: First noun loses el-; the second noun decides definiteness.
• Work clothes = Lebes el-shu8ul. Home food = Akel el-bait. Kitchen's table = Tawlet el-matba5.

sections.heading: Noun possessives › Chain possession pattern
lines: Thing → owner → owner …; only the last noun decides definiteness.
• My friend's sister's book = Ktab u5t sadiqi. The car's work chair = Kursi seyyaret el-shu8ul. The family's bedroom's light = Dawu 8urfet noam el-3aile.

sections.heading: Noun possessives › Describing professions
lines: Profession first, then the specification: Doktoar snaan (dentist), M3allem 3arabi (Arabic teacher), Ustaaz Farsi (Farsi teacher).
With "the", el- goes on the specification: Doktoar el-3yoon, M3allem el3arabi, Ustaaz el-englizi.
A pronoun on the first noun already makes it specific, no el-: Doctoarhom elsnaan, M3almi el3arabi, Ustaazo elfarsi.

sections.heading: Noun + adjective definition
lines: Adjectives go after the noun: Bait kbeer (big house), Seyyara 2adeema (old car), 8urfe ndeefa (clean room).
Known noun: el- on the noun, not on the adjective (a statement): El-bet 7elwa (the girl is beautiful), Hadi el-blooze kum, 3ailetna kbeera. A noun ending in a pronoun is definite by default.
To define the noun (a phrase, not a statement): el- on noun AND adjective: el-lebes el-jdeed (the new clothes), el-kursi el-3aali, el-fus6aan el8aali.

sections.heading: Time and clock
lines: Waqt = the actual time; Saa3a = clock / hour / watch; Marra = turn.
"The time is …" = El-saa3a + feminine number: wa7de (1), tentain (2), talaate (3) …
Minutes: add u/w + number: El-saa3a talaate u 3ashara (3:10), Elsaa3a wa7de u 5amse (1:05).
Rube3 = quarter past; Noss = half past; Ella rube3 = quarter to.
Singular / dual / plural: d2ee2a, D2ee2tain, d2aaye2 (minutes); saanie, Saaneitain, Sawaani (seconds); Saa3a, Saa3tain, Sa3aat (hours). 3:02 = El-saa3a talaate u d2ee2tain.
"At" a time = 3ala: 3ala elsaa3a 3ashara (at 10:00).
What time is it? = Qaddaish el-saa3a / Shu el saa3a. What time is dinner? = Ay saa3a el-3asha?

sections.heading: Emotions / adjectives
lines: Adjectives usually take "min": Ana 5aayef minnak/ek (scared of you), Heyye mitdaay2a minno (upset with him), Humme ma7roojeen minna (embarrassed of us).
Others: 2al2aan (worried) + 3ala; Mishtaa2 (missing) + la; Mu5talef / 8eir (different) + 3an.

sections.heading: Emotions / adjectives › Plural forms
lines: Masculine/general plural: + "een" (Humme mabsoo6een). Feminine plural: + "aat" (Humme 7anoonaat).

sections.heading: Emotions / adjectives › Use of "Bakoon"
lines: Bakoon = I am usually / I tend to be / I will be / I would be. It adds habit, future or conditional meaning.
• Normal present: no "to be", no bakoon: Ana ta3baan (I'm tired), Huwwe jaahez (he's ready).
• Habitual: Bakoon + adjective: Ana bakoon kasool ba3ed el-shu8ul; Marrat heyye betkoon ju3aane billail; E7na benkoon mash8uleen yoam el-etnain.
• Future: Bukra beykoon mabsoo6; Ra7 akoon mitwatter el-usboo3 el-jaay.
• Conditional: Ana bakoon mitdaay2a iza ma btiji ma3i; Heyye betkoon mad8oo6a lamma ykoon 3endha shu8ul kteer.
"when" (lamma) and "if" (iza) signal a conditional sentence → use bakoon / ykoon.

sections.heading: Use of Kul
lines: All = kul + el- (kul el-yoam, kul el-naas, kul el-usboo3). Every / each = kul without el- (kul yoam, kul 7ada, kul usboo3).

sections.heading: Verb "b" prefix elimination
lines: The b- prefix (ba7ki, bitshoof, biroou7) marks the present indicative: real, habitual, happening now.
Drop the b- when the action is uncertain, desired, or dependent on another word:
• Intent / necessity: Biddi ashrab; Lazim tertaa7; Mumkin asa3dak?
• Time conjunctions: Abel-ma yiju; Ba3ed-ma teshra7i; Lamma a6la3; Humme ra7 yjibu el-3asha ma3hom.
• Purpose: La- (Beddi aru7 3ala el-dukkan la-ashtri khobez); 3ashaan (Ana beddi ashufo 3ashan a7kilo eshi).
• Compound verbs: first verb carries tense, second has no b-: Ana baballesh amshi …; Huwwe beyjarreb ye3mal ryaada aktar; E7na ma bne2dar n5alli el-baab maftoo7 bellail.

• Chain reaction: after a gatekeeper (Biddi, Ba7eb, ra7, Laazim) everything joined by u / wala / aw stays without b-: Ana ba7eb a66alla3 3ala el-njoom u a7ki ma3ha; Ma ba3ref a7ki 3arabi wala aktubo; Beddak tiji 3alinna aw e7na niji 3alaik.
Keep the b- after "enno" (that): it starts a new real sentence: Ana bazonn enno ma bey7ebna; Ba3raf enno bteshte8li hoan.

sections.heading: Pointer rule
lines: If the object comes before the verb, the verb needs a pointer pronoun (-o him/it, -ha her/it) linking back.
• Superlatives (Aktar, A7san, Aswa2, A2al): Aktar eshi basawwih; A7san wa7de ba3rafha; Shu aswa2 tamrin bte3malo; Hadi a2al akleh bnetbo5ha; Min a7san zboon bteshte8el ma3o.
• Ay / Kul move the object to the front: Ay 7ada bashufo; Kul kursi byishteruh; Ay makaan benru7 3alaih; Kul sadiq bnelte2i ma3o; Ay mat3am betfadlu taaklu fih.
• Introducing indefinite nouns: Fi zalame ma ba3rafo barra; 3endo tilfizion ma byista5demo; Lamma tlaa2u eshi bet7ebbuh; Beddhom felem ye7daruh; Laazem tlaa2u eshi te3maluh.
